description: Every known bypass, enforcement gap, and policy loophole in GLM-5.1 UI. used=true means the loophole is currently active or available in the default deployment; used=false means it exists but is off, closed, or not applicable by default.

legend.used: true = loophole is in effect or callable right now with default settings
legend.used_false: false = loophole exists as an option but is disabled, blocked, or not reachable by default

loopholes.name: Guard disabled on startup
loopholes.description: RestrictionGuard.check() returns allowed immediately when mode is disabled. Default is disabled in config/local.json and .env.example.

loopholes.name: Log-only guard mode
loopholes.description: Violations are logged but allowed=true is forced. Callable via POST /api/guard/mode or Restrictions tab.

loopholes.name: skip_guard on chat API
loopholes.description: ChatRequest.skip_guard=true bypasses the guard even when mode is enforce.

loopholes.name: Runtime guard disable (no auth)
loopholes.description: POST /api/guard/mode can set disabled or log_only without authentication.

loopholes.name: Agent endpoint unguarded
loopholes.description: /api/agent/run never calls guard.check(). Primary Agent tab uses this path.

loopholes.name: PC Builder unguarded
loopholes.description: /api/pc-builder/build and /stream have no restriction guard.

loopholes.name: Direct tools API unguarded
loopholes.description: POST /api/tools/run executes any agent tool (terminal, write_file, web_search) with no guard.

loopholes.name: Direct workspace write unguarded
loopholes.description: POST /api/workspace/file writes files with no restriction guard.

loopholes.name: Verify API unguarded
loopholes.description: POST /api/verify/run runs checkers with no guard or auth.

loopholes.name: Keyword-only guard (evasion)
loopholes.description: Guard uses order-independent substring keyword matching only. Paraphrasing, synonyms, or other languages can evade blocks.

loopholes.name: Single-message guard scope
loopholes.description: Chat endpoints only check the last user message, not system prompts or full conversation history.

loopholes.name: Test config guard_mode ignored
loopholes.description: restrictions-test.json specifies guard_mode enforce but runtime uses whatever mode is currently set.

local_and_usage.label: Local mode, API keys, and usage limits

loopholes.name: Local mode default
loopholes.description: LOCAL_MODE=true by default — runs on local Ollama without cloud subscription rules.

loopholes.name: No API key for local inference
loopholes.description: requires_api_key is false; Ollama accepts placeholder key local.

loopholes.name: Placeholder API key accepted
loopholes.description: resolve_api_key returns local for localhost URLs without validating a real key.

loopholes.name: Unlimited usage (no rate limiting)
loopholes.description: usage_limits.enabled is false and no rate-limit code exists. Documented as allowed in restrictions/allowed.json.

loopholes.name: Per-request provider override
loopholes.description: All endpoints accept api_key, base_url, and model from the client body, bypassing server .env.

loopholes.name: Cloud requires_api_key not enforced
loopholes.description: coding-agent.json and ai-creation.json mark cloud providers as requires_api_key but backend never blocks missing keys.

loopholes.name: Unlimited usage explicitly allowed
loopholes.description: restrictions/allowed.json includes local-unlimited-usage as an allowed category by design.

loopholes.name: INTERNET_ENABLED flag unused
loopholes.description: settings.internet_enabled is exposed in /api/config but never checked before web_search or fetch_url.

loopholes.name: Frontend internet toggle cosmetic
loopholes.description: settings.internetEnabled is stored in localStorage only and never sent to the backend.

loopholes.name: Agent UI shows internet on always
loopholes.description: AgentPanel hardcodes internet on in the status bar regardless of internetEnabled setting.

loopholes.name: requires_internet not enforced
loopholes.description: requires_internet flags in configs are informational only.

loopholes.name: CORS wildcard in local mode
loopholes.description: allow_origins includes * when local_mode is true — any origin can call the API.

loopholes.name: No API authentication
loopholes.description: No auth middleware on any endpoint.

loopholes.name: Bind all interfaces (0.0.0.0)
loopholes.description: HOST=0.0.0.0 in .env.example — API reachable from LAN if port is open.

loopholes.name: fetch_url SSRF to internal hosts
loopholes.description: fetch_url allows http/https to any host including localhost and private IPs — no blocklist.

loopholes.name: Web search unrestricted
loopholes.description: web_search has no content filtering and no guard check before querying DuckDuckGo.

loopholes.name: Missing checkers count as pass
loopholes.description: Uninstalled linters return passed=true with a note. If all checkers skip, zero_errors is still true.

loopholes.name: No file edits skips verify gate
loopholes.description: block_until_clean only applies when edited_files is non-empty. Agent can finish without ever running verify_code.

loopholes.name: Max fix rounds cap
loopholes.description: After max_fix_rounds (default 5) the agent can finish even if checkers still fail.

loopholes.name: Text-only verify claim
loopholes.description: Agent can finish if assistant text matches verify|test|pass|success|zero errors without running checkers.

loopholes.name: Disable auto-verify via config
loopholes.description: Setting zero_errors_policy.enabled to false in code-checkers.json disables post-edit verification.

loopholes.name: Disable done-blocking via config
loopholes.description: Setting block_agent_done_until_clean to false allows agent completion with checker failures.

loopholes.name: Minimal terminal blocklist
loopholes.description: Only 7 command patterns blocked (rm -rf /, mkfs, fork bomb, dd, shutdown, reboot, halt).

loopholes.name: Substring-only command blocking
loopholes.description: Blocklist uses substring match — variants like rm -rf ~, curl|bash, nc -e, pip install are not blocked.

loopholes.name: shell=True unrestricted shell
loopholes.description: run_terminal uses shell=True — pipelines, redirects, substitution, and env vars all allowed.

loopholes.name: Delete files via terminal
loopholes.description: coding-agent.json sets file_operations.delete false but run_terminal can rm any file in workspace.

loopholes.name: Install packages via terminal
loopholes.description: Training says never install without asking but run_terminal allows pip install, npm install, apt, etc.

loopholes.name: Arbitrary workspace root
loopholes.description: POST /api/workspace/root sets workspace to any directory on disk with no allowlist.

loopholes.name: Feature flags not enforced at runtime
loopholes.description: coding-agent.json features.*.enabled (terminal, web_search, delete, etc.) are never read — all tools always registered.

loopholes.name: Path traversal within workspace blocked
loopholes.description: resolve_safe_path rejects paths that escape workspace root — this protection is active.

loopholes.name: Client overrides max iterations
loopholes.description: AgentRequest.max_iterations overrides the default 30 — client can set very high values.

loopholes.name: Client can disable auto-index
loopholes.description: auto_index=false skips project brief and auto file attachment.

loopholes.name: Client system prompt override
loopholes.description: Frontend can inject custom systemPrompt into chat messages, prepended before backend trained prompt logic.

loopholes.name: Client overrides temperature and tokens
loopholes.description: temperature, max_tokens, and thinking_enabled are fully client-controlled per request.

loopholes.name: Arbitrary test config path
loopholes.description: TestRunRequest.config_path can load any JSON file path from the client.

loopholes.name: No request rate limiting
loopholes.description: No throttling on chat, agent, tools, or verify endpoints.

loopholes.name: Thinking mode unrestricted
loopholes.description: thinking_enabled can be toggled by client with no guard or policy check.

loopholes.name: Stream endpoints share chat guard gaps
loopholes.description: /api/chat/stream uses same skip_guard and single-message guard as non-stream chat.

items.name: Path traversal blocked
items.note: Listed above under terminal_and_workspace — used=false means the bypass is NOT available

items.name: rm -rf / blocked
items.note: Specific pattern rm -rf / is blocked in run_terminal

highest_impact_bypass_paths: Use Agent tab — guard never runs
Guard disabled by default in local.json and .env.example
POST /api/guard/mode with disabled or log_only — no auth
POST /api/chat with skip_guard true when guard is enforce
POST /api/tools/run — direct shell, files, web with no guard
Uninstall linters — verify reports ZERO ERRORS YES
Mention verify or pass in agent text without running checkers
internetEnabled checkbox does nothing — web tools always work
